what: English sentences that a locale renders more than one way, as the files contain them. Nothing here was written by this process; it is a reading.
how_to_use: Compare a suspect locale file against the renderings listed for that language. A file that reproduces the split - the same sentence rendered two ways at the same two keys - shares our history. A file that carries only one rendering per sentence still has to have picked one of ours.
caveats: Describes the tree at the commit named above. Later edits move it; released artefacts on PyPI and the public git history carry the older state with a third-party timestamp, which is what dates it.
Label splits are weaker evidence than phrase splits: a one-word key often differs because the word has two senses, which any translator would reproduce. Phrase splits are arbitrary choices.
This is a record, not a claim of correctness. Some splits are inconsistencies worth fixing. Fixing one does not weaken the record, which is dated to before the fix.
